clue.text: He quits group sex when Cyclops enters — boring

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the setter's letter goes into the shortened word
someone who quits a group leaves it, so the pronoun walks out of the word for group sex

parts.note: taken as written; these are the letters removed
Cyclops is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A tired grumble that an orgy goes flat once the crossword setter turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often refers to himself as I, and Cyclops is Private Eye's setter. The I lands just after the first letter of the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome wearies people through tedium, which is exactly what a boring thing does.

clue.text: Bush to Blair: "Surrender, so war ends? That's awful!"

indicators.note: the ends of the preceding words are wanted, so only the final letter of each is kept

explanation.surface: Bush urging Blair to give up so the Iraq war can finish, met with a cry of dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' seems to belong to the war, but it applies to every word before it, from Bush to war.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is uttered as an exclamation of shock or dismay, the same as crying out that something is dreadful.

clue.text: Straw's heart set on an honour and stately attire

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the five-letter name
Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Foreign Secretary Jack Straw longing for a gong and the finery that goes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was Blair's Foreign Secretary. In a down clue, one piece 'set on' another sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long formal garment worn on ceremonial occasions, the kind of dress worn in state.

clue.text: Nigel, a stickler, able to endure a stretch inside

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words, spanning the name and the next word

explanation.surface: A strict man named Nigel who could bear a spell in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch inside' reads as a prison sentence, but 'inside' is the hiding signal and the stretch belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material can be pulled out and spring back, so it tolerates being extended without breaking.

clue.text: Distorting the creed with nation's extremes: descriptive of, say, Ian Paisley's position

definitions.text: descriptive of, say, Ian Paisley's position

indicators.note: distorting twists something out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: Twisting religious belief with nationalism, as a Northern Ireland firebrand might.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley was the hardline Ulster Unionist preacher and politician known for refusing to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrenched position is dug in and immovable, a fair description of Paisley's famously unyielding stance.

clue.text: The devil's own erection incorporating fancy bell

indicators.note: fancy means elaborately made up, so the letters are rearranged
incorporating means taking into the body, so the rearranged letters go inside

explanation.surface: Satan's arousal somehow involving an ornamental bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The devil's own' reads as the start of the joke, but it is the definition: something born in the devil's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellborn means sprung from the infernal regions, so it describes what belongs to Satan himself.

clue.text: Sulphur content of piss of Bruno

indicators.note: a content sits within its container, so one element goes inside the other word

explanation.surface: A lab report on the sulphur level in a urine sample from someone called Bruno, perhaps the boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruno is a stock name for a bear in children's stories, so 'of Bruno' is 'of a bear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursine means relating to bears, and Bruno stands for a bear, so of Bruno is bearlike.

clue.text: Incompetent US agents have sod all but this parting remark

parts.note: the Central Intelligence Agency; 'Incompetent' is the setter's jibe
nothing, the letter shaped like zero

explanation.surface: A sneer that the bungling American spies have achieved nothing but a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is the Italian farewell, used casually in English as a way to say goodbye when leaving.

clue.text: Alternative leader of Labour? Gordon's mostly lacking the fibre

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept
lacking most of itself, the name keeps only a small remnant

explanation.surface: Speculation about a rival to Blair, with Gordon Brown said to lack moral fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: GORDON loses most of itself, GORD, keeping ON. Gordon Brown was Blair's heir apparent as Labour leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlon is a trademark acrylic textile fibre, used in knitwear as a wool substitute.

clue.text: Labour to get organ (Sun, finally?)

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

explanation.surface: The Labour Party seeking to win over the Sun newspaper as its mouthpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party, as in the surface; here it is the verb, to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain money or reward by working, which is to labour in order to obtain.

clue.text: People who want unknown, dodgy ways to make a living

parts.words: dodgy ways to make a living
parts.note: in British slang a 'nice little earner' is a profitable, often shady, racket

explanation.surface: A description of people drawn to obscure, shady means of making money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who yearns longs for something, so yearners are those who desire or crave things.

clue.text: What the rucked-up carpet had to be after soldiers shagged?

definitions.text: What the rucked-up carpet had to be

explanation.surface: Soldiers have had sex on a carpet and left it rumpled, so it needs putting back down.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpled carpet must be put down again flat, which is to be laid a second time.

clue.text: Court rip off taking place, as you'd find in a rotten borough?

definitions.text: as you'd find in a rotten borough

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: an event that is on is happening

explanation.surface: A legal swindle going ahead, the kind of thing a decaying town council might see.
explanation.walkthrough: A rotten borough was a pre-1832 English constituency with a handful of voters, controlled by a patron.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten boroughs were notorious for bribery and patronage, so dishonest dealing is what you would find there.

clue.text: Clary: "I'm up Sid's end — wild party!" …

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order
the end of the name is its last letter, which alone is kept

explanation.surface: Julian Clary making a camp innuendo about a raucous party, as the comedian would.
explanation.walkthrough: Julian Clary is a camp British comedian. Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist political party, so 'party' is a political one, not a wild one.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid Cymru is a political party in Wales, campaigning for Welsh independence.

clue.text: Finished removing top from someone you're shagging?

indicators.note: the top of an across word is its start, so the first letter is taken off

explanation.surface: Sex is done once you have pulled the top off your partner, a deliberately rude image.
explanation.walkthrough: LOVER loses its first letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is over has come to its end, so it is complete and done with.

clue.text: Dyke wants Beeb's head to intervene in Selina broadcast

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so one letter goes into the middle of the rest
broadcast also means scattered widely, so the name's letters are strewn into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

explanation.surface: A gay activist demanding the BBC's director-general step into a programme presented by Selina Scott.
explanation.walkthrough: Beeb is the nickname for the BBC. Selina Scott was a British TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyke is a slang, sometimes reclaimed, term for a woman attracted to women.

clue.text: … onwards and upwards from this point for mean gay?

definitions.text: onwards and upwards from this point

explanation.surface: Continuing the Clary joke: the party goes upwards from here for a mean gay man.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the previous clue; 'mean' looks like 'intend' but means low and nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers set out from a base camp and climb ever higher, so everything ahead lies above it.

clue.text: Old fashioned you accepting hand job (wife having left) — I'm grateful in a quaint way

definitions.text: I'm grateful in a quaint way

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the old pronoun holds the other piece
the wife leaves, so her abbreviation walks out of the word

explanation.surface: An archaic speaker thanking someone for a sexual favour once the spouse has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old fashioned' looks like it describes the hand job, but it goes with 'you' to give the archaic pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Thankee is a dialect or old-fashioned form of thank you, a rustic expression of gratitude.

clue.text: Organ placed by disrespectful female at one end of microscope

parts.note: a demeaning slang word for a woman

explanation.surface: A sexist scientist peering down a microscope at a sexual organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyepiece is the lens you look through at the top of a microscope, opposite the objective.

clue.text: Who's bi? Dicky, at the last luvvies' thing

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for unsound or shaky, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Theatrical gossip about who is bisexual, with a smutty name, Dicky, dropped in.
explanation.walkthrough: Luvvies is British slang for actors and theatre people, mocked as gushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Showbiz, short for show business, is the world of entertainment that luvvies inhabit.

clue.text: One who sacrificed himself, pointlessly, for sex

indicators.note: without a point, meaning a compass point is dropped from the name

parts.note: Captain Oates, who walked out into the blizzard on Scott's Antarctic expedition

explanation.surface: A cynical aside that someone threw their life away just for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' looks like 'in vain', but it is OATES without one compass point, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting your oats is British slang for having sex, so the plural noun stands for it.

clue.text: Luvvies' award back to front and behind

indicators.note: what is at the back is brought round to the front, so the last letter moves to the start

parts.note: the British Academy Film and Television award

explanation.surface: A film prize being held the wrong way round and from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: BAFTA's final A moves to the front. 'back to front' wants to mean a full reversal, but that gives ATFAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical term for towards the stern, meaning to the rear of a vessel.

clue.text: He'd try, dead pissed, to be wet no more

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger out of order

explanation.surface: A drunk vowing to dry out and stop being a wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dehydrated has had all its water removed, leaving it dry rather than moist.

clue.text: Labour's number two gets in to abolish periodical

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the letter goes inside the verb
the party's number two is its second letter, which alone is kept

explanation.surface: Labour's deputy leader winning power so as to scrap a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number two' looks like the deputy leader, John Prescott in Blair's day; it is the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book or publication issued once a year, a kind of periodical.

clue.text: A bit like a pirate, having pee before capsizing yacht?

indicators.note: a capsizing boat is overturned and jumbled, so the word's letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor relieving himself before the yacht overturns, rather piratical behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Stage pirates wear an eye-patch, so being patchy makes you a bit like one. 'pee' is the name of the letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Read playfully, patchy means wearing a patch, the eye-patch that marks a stage pirate.

clue.text: Joker, performing, pissed on sleeper

explanation.surface: A drunk comedian urinating on someone asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pissed on' reads as one rude phrase; pissed is drunk and 'on' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon-lit is a sleeping car on a continental European train, a railway sleeper.

clue.text: Austrian town's pisspoor rag 'annexing' Zeitung's leader

indicators.note: something pisspoor is badly done, so these letters are botched into a new order
annexing means attaching, so one piece is tacked on to the end of the other
the leader of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

explanation.surface: A dismal local newspaper in an Austrian town swallowing a German daily.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeitung is German for newspaper; rag is slang for a poor-quality paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Graz is a city in south-eastern Austria, the country's second largest.

clue.text: Dam Scotland Yard's arse over tip

indicators.note: falling arse over tip means going head over heels, so the word is turned the other way round

parts.note: the Met, London's Metropolitan Police, based at Scotland Yard

explanation.surface: A curse at the London police for taking a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' looks like a misspelt curse, but it is the verb meaning to block a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or check it, which is what damming a river does.

clue.text: Indian dish sustains one in hurricane

indicators.note: to sustain is to hold up, so the storm holds the number within itself

parts.note: Hurricane Rita, which struck the US Gulf Coast in 2005

explanation.surface: Curry keeping someone going through a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: Atlantic hurricanes take personal names; Rita came weeks after Katrina in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yoghurt side dish from South Asian cooking, served with curries.

clue.text: Cunning liar ditches Brenda

indicators.note: ditching something means getting rid of it, so those letters are thrown out

parts.note: Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and peer jailed for perjury
Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose cipher is ER

explanation.surface: A sly perjurer dumping a woman named Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls Queen Elizabeth Brenda; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch can mean knowingly mischievous or sly, as in an arch smile, a sense close to crafty.
